# Clouseau

Clouseau also provides a centrally maintained local agent skill and signed review
receipts. Agent-only installation is independent of CI: it uses authenticated
coding harnesses and creates no Actions configuration or provider secrets.
Inside Claude Code, Codex or opencode the calling agent supplies the review
sessions (`--agent`); the headless `--harness` form is for a plain terminal.
Local AI review runs regardless of coverage percentage or availability and keeps
its quality verdict separate from real verification results. Opted-in CI verifies
an enrolled runner's passing AI receipt without repeating the review, then still
requires its own tests and exact coverage before approval/merge. See
[local review, installation and trust boundaries](docs/local-review.md).
Consumers without accepted recipe/enrollment/workflows use the separate
[initial owner-authorized trust installation](docs/initial-installation.md).
Its signed evidence cannot approve ordinary changes or automatically merge.
Clouseau's own accepted-policy bootstrap and native coverage diagnostics are
documented in [self-review](docs/self-review.md).

Shared coverage gates and evidence-led AI pull request approval for GitHub Actions.
Clouseau owns the PR intent review process: check whether a change is needed,
compare it with repository contracts and precedent, request the owner's second
opinion when necessary, and approve and arm auto-merge only after every technical
requirement passes. The initial implementation was extracted from Colombo.

Version 2 implements the [change acceptance protocol](docs/change-acceptance.md):
product fit, need and proportionality; nine-factor technical findings; independent
source investigations; a persistent evidence ledger; bounded repairs; and native
protected auto-merge. Humans decide genuine purpose and authority questions.
Technical uncertainty goes to automated investigation and cannot be waived by
an intent comment. Version 1 remains explicit compatibility for existing pins.

## Ownership

Clouseau contains the coverage checker, regression tests, PR intent review rules,
DeepSeek integration, approval controller, and reusable composite action.
Each consuming repository keeps its build/test commands, a configuration file,
and its own purpose, contracts, acceptance criteria, and manual-review owner.
There is no application-specific deployment infrastructure in Clouseau.

## Operations

Automatic CI integrations pin the small `gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve`
bootstrap once at a reviewed full commit. It selects protected Clouseau main,
freezes its SHA and computes its digest. Every engine job checks out that SHA
and invokes the local action with the same trusted outputs. Normal central
releases need no consumer pin or digest update. See [automatic CI upgrades](docs/automatic-ci-upgrades.md)
for source authorization, failure behavior and exact local-receipt compatibility.
Legacy fixed installations may still use `gaulatti/clouseau@FULL_REVIEWED_COMMIT_SHA`;
upgrading those installations requires a reviewed PR. See `examples/colombo.json`
for the version 2 policy configuration.

| Operation | Inputs | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |

| `coverage` | Accepted-base v2 `coverage-config`, or legacy `coverage-report` + `source-directory` with optional `coverage-format` | Require exact, nonempty 100% native application line and branch coverage; the two input forms are mutually exclusive |

For example, a caller's coverage step supplies:

```yaml
with:
  operation: coverage
  coverage-report: coverage.json
  source-directory: src
```

The report must contain every compiled application path, including uncovered
code. Vendor/dependency coverage cannot mask application gaps. Counts must match
exactly; rounded percentages, missing data, or a zero branch total fail. The
caller owns instrumentation and test execution. Colombo uses Rust nightly branch
instrumentation with normal application cfgs, followed by docs and Docker tests.

For JavaScript/TypeScript, select `coverage-format: istanbul` and pass the native
`coverage-final.json` produced by c8/Istanbul. Set `source-directory` to the
original application source tree, not compiled output. Every `.ts`, `.tsx`,
`.js`, `.jsx`, `.cjs`, and `.mjs` source must appear, including unloaded modules.
Declaration-only `.d.ts` files, concrete test conventions and dependency
directories are not application sources; generated application code remains
included. The fixed inventory conventions and multi-artifact configuration are
documented in [local coverage plans](docs/local-review.md#multiple-native-coverage-artifacts).
The checker rejects omitted,
duplicate, mismatched, skipped or malformed measurements and coverage-ignore
directives. It derives exact line and branch totals from native hit counters,
never from rounded summary percentages. Configure c8 `--all` over all compiled
JavaScript with source maps to measure unloaded TypeScript sources. Run real
runtime tests as well as unit tests; this format support does not replace them.

For Python, select `coverage-format: coveragepy` and supply the unmodified JSON
format 3 report from `coverage.py` with branch measurement enabled. See the
[native Python coverage contract](docs/python-coverage.md) for source inventory,
report generation, path binding and exact native counter validation. This reads
coverage.py's executable lines and branch decision exits, not statement
percentages or every traced transition. Empty global totals, omitted application
modules, exclusions, partial coverage and inconsistent counters fail closed.

For Go, select `coverage-format: go` and supply the `go test -coverprofile` text
profile built with `-coverpkg=./...`. Go records statements and basic blocks only, so
`lines` means statements and `branches` means basic blocks; implicit false exits and
short-circuit operands are not measured. See the [native Go coverage
contract](docs/go-coverage.md) for exact semantics, inventory and failures.

Monorepos may use the accepted-base version 2 local recipe with separate native
Istanbul, coverage.py and Go parts. `operation: coverage` accepts that recipe through
`coverage-config` and uses the shared per-part and aggregate measurement rules.
The CI gate requires each part to be complete and exact; local AI can assess
honest partial or unavailable measurements. There is no consumer-side report
merging. Legacy single-report inputs remain supported.

## Trust and permissions

Keep test execution and privileged review in separate jobs. Contributor code runs
on disposable read-only PR runners with no secrets. Assessment and gating must
check out only the protected base branch; configuration, README, and repository
contract files are read from that trusted checkout. PR patches, source, commit
messages, and tickets are untrusted evidence and never executed by the reviewer.

The `assess` job needs actions/contents/pull-requests/issues read permissions and
the repository's `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`. `gate` needs contents/pull-requests/issues/
actions write permissions and must receive no provider key. Pass the
assessment output between jobs. The action cannot elevate the caller's token.
Version 1's shared model is `deepseek-flash`; changes are sent to it only after
technical verification succeeds. It assesses repository fit and supported intent,
including large test improvements. There is no file-count or line-count approval
cutoff. New product decisions and unclear scope require the owner’s judgment.
A missing or token-truncated provider completion is retried within the same
read-only assessment, using the identical evidence, at most three attempts total.
Retries wait one then two seconds. The output budget starts at 4,096 tokens and
doubles only after a token-limit truncation, capped at 16,384 tokens per request.
Every request retains its 90-second timeout. Fixed attempt/outcome/token-budget
categories are logged without model text, reasoning, patches, or credentials.
A complete verdict stops retries immediately, including second opinions,
integrity rejections, and invalid or wrong-revision evidence. HTTP failures,
network/decoding errors, unknown terminal finish reasons, and exhausted retries
fail closed and require a second opinion. The provider health probe is unchanged. AI must also support test integrity with evidence about assertions
and failure cases. Detected test fakery blocks approval, including after an intent
confirmation. Coverage percentages alone cannot satisfy that assessment. No numerical confidence score grants approval.

`sensitive_paths` lists additional paths the consumer explicitly protects with
owner confirmation. The example leaves it empty; ordinary test, dependency,
and infrastructure paths are assessed by AI rather than rejected by filename.
The configured verification workflow, review controls, and repository-purpose
contract remain protected. Their changes still receive an AI integrity assessment
and require explicit owner confirmation.

The native protected merge path requires active effective base-branch rules: strict required
checks for the configured verification job and native `approve-and-merge` job
from GitHub Actions, a fresh approving review, no deletion, and no force pushes. The installing
administrator must also verify no bypass actors. Repository auto-merge and Actions
approving reviews must be enabled for automatic merge. Runtime tokens do not get administration access.

Protocol v2 also supports explicit `"merge_mode": "manual"` in accepted base
configuration. Repository auto-merge must be disabled in this mode, including
for owner-authored PRs. Tests, exact coverage, review, source binding and
current-head code-owner approval for external contributors when CODEOWNERS is configured remain mandatory.
Available branch protection is still enforced. Only GitHub's specific HTTP 403
private-plan upgrade response, together with verified private visibility and an
unprotected branch, permits approval without host-enforced protection. Generic
permission failures, unavailable APIs, public unprotected repositories and
incomplete available rules fail closed. The summary states when GitHub cannot
enforce the checks; trusted maintainers must honor them before manually merging.
The controller never merges or dispatches deployment in manual mode.

This repository explicitly selects `"merge_mode": "automatic"` for strict owner-only automation:
CODEOWNERS must exist on the accepted base and the author must own every affected
path. The normal protected native flow is unchanged. On the exact unavailable
private-plan condition above, native repository auto-merge stays disabled while
the validated acceptance controller can atomically fast-forward the exact base
to the reviewed head, with paired source/base compare-and-swap and no force.
This supports same-repository branches with an up-to-date head only; other
contributions remain manual. Missing/stale reviews, failed full verification or
coverage, changed revisions and API errors cannot authorize that write. This is
controller-enforced delivery, not unavailable native branch protection. See
[the complete private-plan contract](docs/change-acceptance.md#controller-enforced-owner-merge-on-an-unavailable-private-plan),
including deployment-trigger limitations. Omitting `merge_mode` preserves the
existing native flow and optional CODEOWNERS behavior.

Manual decisions assign the PR to `manual_reviewer` and request that person's
review. Owner-authored PRs use assignment without an invalid self-review request.
The owner can comment `/approve-intent FULL_HEAD_SHA`; this confirms intent only.
An owner confirmation can carry the actual accepted requirement, rather than
leaving investigators to infer it from a revision alone:

```text
/approve-intent FULL_HEAD_SHA

Accepted purpose:
Describe the accepted outcome and its boundaries.
```

Clouseau authenticates the configured owner and current permission, binds the
literal requirement to that revision and revalidates it before writing. Ordinary
PR prose remains untrusted; every mechanism still earns its own justification.
An agent delegated to install an accepted scope may record these confirmations
on the owner's behalf through its repairs without repeated approval prompts.
All tests and exact coverage remain mandatory. Changes invalidate the decision.
The Actions bot cannot approve its own PR; it needs an independent human review.
First-time fork workflow authorization remains GitHub's responsibility.

The PR report starts with a plain-language decision, one conservative scorecard,
and one entry per causal technical finding. Each entry shows its consequence,
blocking score, affected area, evidence and required outcome. Reviewer
disagreements, product rework, missing evidence and owner decisions stay visible.
The lowest product scores across all material changes and both reviewers are
shown; unrelated good scores never compensate for a failing change. Optional
findings show expected benefit and optional priority without creating a blocker.

Expand **Scoring and evidence** for the unchanged formulas, every individual
grade and explanation, both independent reviews, persistent finding history and
the evidence register (source and line ranges). Source text is not copied into PR
comments; the complete source-bound record stays in the run's acceptance artifact.
Large audits retain lossless evidence pages. Summary
formatting uses the already validated record and makes no model requests. A
review decision never claims that merge, deployment or live verification finished.

The display regression includes the actual public Palazzo #27 review, linked to
its immutable signed evidence. Its original comment contains 36,564 characters;
5,388 remain visible with evidence sections closed. The new overview contains
948 visible characters, over five times shorter, with the same approved
verdict, both reviewers' 100/100 product scores and no technical findings. This
is an offline display fixture, never a substitute for fresh review or CI evidence.

Version 2 additionally uploads `work/clouseau-acceptance*.json` as a run/attempt
bound artifact and downloads it into `work/` in the separate approval and repair
jobs. Select examiner, challenger and grader explicitly in `acceptance`; see
[the self-hosting configuration](.github/clouseau.json). `typesafe-key` is needed
only when the explicit Jev/DeepSeek grading route is selected. Failure never
silently changes that choice. A separate repair job receives an independent
author token through `repair-token`; Colombo reuses its existing deployment
token. Neither the approval job nor AI inspection receives that author token. The repair
job requires a trusted GitHub head repository matching the base repository before
loading the author credential; the writer independently rechecks that identity.
Only purpose/authority decisions can use owner confirmation in version 2.

The consumer must retain PR, metadata-only target, comment, and manual workflow
entry points and PR-level concurrency. The controller validates the exact latest
PR-event run, revision, verification job, and named steps from configuration.
The read-only `assess` job waits for the PR verification run to finish before
calling AI. That wait occupies a runner, and a verification job that is queued
behind it on a single-slot pool can never start, so the wait is bounded by
progress (see "Waiting for verification" in `docs/automatic-ci-upgrades.md`). Allow 70 minutes for this job when verification can take 60 minutes.
The separate native job named `approve-and-merge` calls `gate`; it must run on
`pull_request_target` and fail if assessment fails, intent is missing, integrity
is rejected, or technical evidence is incomplete. Use `always()` with `needs`
so a failed assessment cannot silently skip the required gate. In other event
contexts, use a different job name to avoid a skipped duplicate required check.
The `native-gate` and `wait-for-verification` action inputs default to `true`.

The native job summary preserves detailed reasons; no additional API check is
created in native mode. A `GITHUB_TOKEN` API check can attach to another run's
suite and is insufficient as the required approval result for this flow. Comment/manual handlers call
`request-reassessment` with actions write and contents/pull-requests read access;
they rerun the current revision's existing `pull_request_target` run. Its test job
is skipped, so confirming intent does not rebuild the container. The handler
validates maintainer permission and exact comment SHA before requesting a rerun.

Run `finalize` in a separate job after the native gate succeeds, with actions
write and contents/pull-requests read access and no provider key. Auto-merge must
wait for the required gate job to finish, so deployment handoff cannot run inside
that gate. A provider diagnostic remains read-only and never approves a PR.

`deployment` is either `null` or an explicit workflow and path list. For a bot
merge touching those paths, Clouseau dispatches that existing workflow because
`GITHUB_TOKEN` merges suppress push-triggered workflows. It verifies main still
points at the merged revision. Deployment health, staged rollout, smoke tests,
bake windows, and ticket closure remain separate delivery work.

## Development

```sh
node --test src/*.test.cjs
```

Clouseau's own CI also requires exactly 100% line and branch coverage across
all production JavaScript modules. New source files are included
even when no test imports them. Test code is outside the production scope;
there are no exclusions for production failure paths or rounded thresholds.

To run the same gate locally with Node 22:

```sh
./scripts/verify-coverage
```

Clouseau needs only Node. One integration test runs a fixture Python application
under real coverage.py to prove the `coveragepy` adapter against live output, so
install `requirements-test.txt` (coverage.py 7.13.0) to run the whole suite. The
coverage gate itself is `bin/coverage-gate.cjs`
(`check REPORT SOURCE_DIRECTORY [llvm|istanbul|coveragepy|go]` or
`plan ACCEPTED_CONFIG [DIRECTORY]`), so reviewing a Python application requires
Python only for that application's own tests.

Successful native Node runs print compact outcomes and retain complete same-run
traces with per-run hashes; see [native verification traces](docs/native-verification.md).

CI also exercises the packaged composite action and verifies both passing and
failing coverage reports. No provider credential is needed for regression tests.
The new repository's wiki is not initialized; operational documentation lives
here until a wiki is available.

## Live model evaluations

The `evaluate-review` operation calls the real provider with three committed
synthetic review contexts. Maintenance must qualify, unrelated product scope
must request an owner decision, and test-specific validation bypasses must block
approval. A wrong or unavailable decision fails the evaluation. The GitHub and
technical-readiness inputs are fixtures; these evaluations validate model judgment,
not actual test execution or an end-to-end PR merge. The maintenance case injects
one synthetic truncated completion before calling the real provider to verify
automatic recovery within the same assessment. Logs identify that injection
explicitly; it is not evidence of a naturally occurring provider outage. Controller regression tests
use simulated provider decisions separately. Run live evaluations only in a
read-only diagnostic job with the provider key and no repository write token.

## Wiki maintenance after deployment

The [shared wiki policy](policy/wiki-maintenance.md) grounds documentation in the
exact deployment source revision and current wiki. A read-only job plans the
complete page set, generates each page against that common plan, validates links
and navigation, and independently fact-checks every proposed page, including
retained claims. Existing wiki prose can be stale; production control flow takes
precedence. The full bundle must pass before it becomes a publishable artifact.

Planning and writing use DeepSeek Flash; the independent factual checker uses
DeepSeek V4 Pro with low reasoning effort; Flash uses non-thinking mode at
temperature zero. DeepSeek's
[beta strict function-return format](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/tool_calls/)
provides separate schemas for planning, the exact requested page, and factual
review. The sole return name is `wiki_result`. Its arguments are parsed as data;
no model-selected function is executed. Plain-text answers, unknown return names,
multiple returns, and incomplete results fail closed. The factual checker uses
automatic tool choice because the provider forbids forced choices in thinking
mode; a plain answer still fails validation. Token truncation retries
use identical evidence and schemas, at most three attempts with 4,096/8,192/16,384
output tokens and 90-second deadlines. PR review keeps its existing API and
reasoning policy.

Each page receives a dedicated factual audit with the complete source map and
the other proposed pages for consistency. The combined factual report is a fixed
checklist keyed by the planned pages. Each page
has one source reference, a findings string limited to 2,000 characters, and a
supported verdict emitted last. Every page must be supported with no unresolved
findings; contradictory verdicts are rejected. This avoids unbounded evidence
arrays while retaining an independent judgment for every updated page.

Source references select controller-assigned `path:Lnumber` IDs. The native
response schema restricts paths to actual source filenames; shortened basenames
are not accepted. The source map preserves exact lines, including blanks.
Local validation rejects invented IDs, blank citations, and missing page checks.
The model cannot substitute quotation text.
This is an AI quality gate rather than a proof of semantic correctness;
documentation still needs correction when new evidence reveals an error.

A rejected factual draft may receive up to three correction passes from actionable findings.
Only pages with findings are regenerated; other page bytes are preserved. The
complete corrected batch must differ, pass structural/link validation again,
and receive a fresh supporting factual verdict. No previously rejected text is
resubmitted, including cycles between drafts. Missing findings or an exhausted
correction budget stops publication. The
read-only `evaluate-wiki` operation disables correction and calls the real model
on supported authentication and shared-refresh documents plus deliberate
denial/unavailability and FTP-only-refresh falsehoods. Provider, schema, or citation failures cannot count as a successful
negative result.

Live evaluation case diagnostics are saved at `wiki-plan.json.evaluation.json`,
including when a positive or negative control fails. Structured generation
diagnostics are saved beside the plan at
`wiki-plan.json.diagnostic.json`. Rejected planning values are retained before
any generation. Factual diagnostics contain each reviewed draft, findings, and
its immutable source-line map. Consumers should upload diagnostics even when
planning fails. No provider credentials or raw transport bodies are stored.

A separate publisher receives no model key or deployment credentials. It downloads
only its own workflow run's artifact and independently verifies the repository,
source SHA, wiki base SHA, run ID, and the expected main workflow's completed
successful deployment job. Draft generation can skip deployment verification;
publication never can. Generation needs `actions: read` and `contents: read`.
Only publication needs `contents: write` and a Git-authenticated wiki checkout.

Consumer `.github/clouseau-wiki.json` specifies every field explicitly:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "source_paths": ["README.md", "src/", "migrations/", "Dockerfile", "compose.yaml", "Makefile", "scripts/", ".env.example", ".github/workflows/"],
  "deployment_workflow": "backend-deploy.yml",
  "deployment_job": "deploy",
  "wiki_branch": "master"
}
```

Only committed text in those paths is read. Real `.env` files and agent-rule paths
are refused; wiki agent instructions are excluded from model context. The wiki
must be a clean, initialized Git checkout. Pages are flat Markdown filenames,
including Home, `_Sidebar`, and `_Footer`; the model cannot change configuration,
edit `AGENTS.md`, or delete pages. Local limits are twenty pages, 128,000 bytes per
page, 512,000 bytes per bundle, 300 source files, and 1,000,000 bytes per complete
request. Nothing is silently truncated. Unsafe paths, duplicate/ambiguous names,
broken internal links, orphaned new pages, unsupported link syntax, and unclosed
code fences fail validation.

Publication uses a private temporary Git index, never model-directed filesystem
writes. All pages and the `.clouseau-deployment.json` source/run receipt form one
commit. A changed remote wiki base or rejected non-force push publishes nothing;
concurrent human edits are never rebased or overwritten. A repeated source SHA
is idempotent. A new revision with no Markdown changes records a truthful audit
receipt. Serialize deployment and documentation together to prevent a later
release from overtaking documentation. Documentation failure leaves the completed
deployment intact and makes the workflow fail visibly; it does not roll back or
claim external service health, running image bytes, or terminal upload delivery.


### Review reliability and provider qualification

Reviews retain fixed/dismissed findings across pushes and explicitly inventory
inspected, excluded and missing evidence. Missing material context prevents
approval. When protected-base CODEOWNERS exists, protocol v2 enables automatic merge only for code-owner-authored PRs;
other contributions require current-head code-owner approval and manual merge.
Confirmed absence leaves that ownership gate inactive; existing invalid files or
unavailable ownership evidence still block. Other acceptance gates are unchanged.
See [the review contract](docs/change-acceptance.md#review-convergence-and-completeness).

The frozen qualification corpus in `test/acceptance-cases.cjs` includes clean
maintenance, a real executable zero-body regression, product drift, unnecessary
machinery, deceptive tests, a dismissed false allegation and unavailable material
context. Each case has an expected disposition and an evidence-based rationale.
A blocking verdict on an unrelated issue does not qualify the known-defect case.

`node test/evaluate-acceptance.cjs` performs live judgment qualification using the
existing provider credentials and routes. `CLOUSEAU_EVALUATION_GRADERS` selects
`deepseek`, `typesafe` or `routed` (comma-separated for comparisons). Optional
`CLOUSEAU_EVALUATION_CASES` selects named diagnostic cases; such a partial run does
not qualify a replacement. Output records the corpus and protocol fingerprints,
selected cases, route, literal evidence, responses and bounded request usage.
At most 64 provider requests, including historical replay usage, are permitted.
Completed negative decisions are retained, never retried to seek approval.

Recorded-response tests exercise transport parsing, validation, history and
scoring without calling a model. They are deterministic software evidence,
not evidence of a replacement model's review quality. Provider changes require
a complete live corpus qualification against the same frozen inputs and expected
outcomes; no provider is switched automatically by these tests. Replay is allowed
only for unchanged source/policy/routing inputs and is labeled separately from
new live calls. Qualification fixtures do not establish a genuine PR merge.

# Clouseau review contract

Clouseau provides shared, evidence-bound repository change assessment, exact
coverage gates, native PR approval and merge, and deployment-driven wiki updates.
Consumers provide their own protected purpose contract and verification steps.

Local agent review and authenticated receipt reuse serve the same change
acceptance purpose. Agent-only installation and refresh are independent of CI
installation. A protected verifier may reuse an enrolled runner's source-bound
passing review without another AI request, while preserving native tests, exact
coverage, existing owner authority and branch protection. Initial workstation
signing explicitly trusts the enrolled operator and privileged processes; it
does not claim hardware attestation or protection from a compromised runner.

Changes must preserve the trust boundary between untrusted contributor source,
secret-free execution checks, read-only AI evaluation and the separate write
controller. Native protected-main requirements, immutable revision identities,
meaningful tests and exact 100% line and branch coverage are mandatory.
Model text is data. It must never execute as a command or grant permissions.

An explicitly accepted manual-only integration must enforce branch protection
where GitHub makes it available and disable automatic merge for every author.
GitHub's documented private-plan protection limitation may permit independent
review and approval without host-enforced merge blocking, but never automatic
merge, waived tests, lowered coverage or omitted current-head owner approval for
external contributions. Missing credentials or generic API failures are not
evidence of that plan limitation. Report the enforcement boundary truthfully.

Useful defect repairs, meaningful tests, provider qualification and maintenance
serve this purpose without a new product decision. Speculative frameworks,
unrelated capabilities or additional authority require concrete justification.
The shared protocol defines product and technical scoring; no owner intent
confirmation waives integrity failures, incomplete evidence or technical defects.

Changes to the reviewer implementation, scoring policy, verification controls or
this purpose contract require explicit exact-revision confirmation from gaulatti.
Only real purpose, authority and outcome tradeoffs are sent to the owner. A
missing provider response or unresolved code concern belongs to automated
investigation or bounded repair, never automatic approval.

Post-deployment wiki maintenance is a separate, already supported operation.
Source merge, deployment, live health and published documentation remain distinct
results; do not infer one from another.

b9e44488d9d6eec65bb671ec27c47aeae818b608.content:
# Change acceptance protocol, version 2

Clouseau answers two questions independently: does this implementation belong in
the repository, and is there a demonstrated reason it cannot merge? Passing
tests is mandatory evidence; it does not answer either question by itself.

The protected base supplies repository purpose, requirements, configuration and
policy. Every changed file is accounted for. The complete original and proposed
text, linked tickets, recent file precedent and actual verification receipt are
bound to immutable revisions. Fork source is read from the fork at its exact SHA.
Contributor text, source and model output are data, never executable instructions.
Each stored source citation and changed-source anchor is limited to 40 inclusive
lines. The controller partitions a longer valid model-selected interval into
entries within that limit and expands every reference to include all its parts.
Every cited line and judgment is preserved; no model retry is needed for chunking.
Unknown sources, invalid coordinates and unmatched references still stop review.
New investigations select from a controller-generated proof catalog. The tool
schema enumerates those IDs for every citation and changed-source anchor. The
controller generates the stored source register and coordinates; the model
supplies observations and chooses the relevant supplied proofs.
The supplied syntax includes direct source references for every changed file.
File accounting cites the corresponding changed source. An investigator may
observe the lack of a binding requirement without inventing contract authority.
That factual phase produces no approval score. Every positive binding grade still
requires trusted contract proof during final validation and at the write gate.

## Units and gates

The examiner groups the change into units (a `capability` for a user-observable
outcome, a `mechanism` for machinery serving it) so every changed file is
accounted for. Units carry no scores. Unrequested or over-built code is reported
as a finding only when it causes a distinct runtime, data, security,
compatibility or verification failure.

Approval depends only on technical findings and gates: a finding scoring 70 or
more must be fixed, a violated gate blocks, and nothing else does.

Linked requirements have content-addressed entries in the same proof catalog as
repository sources. Investigators can cite their actual text, URL and author so
the atomic grader receives the request itself. Issue content remains untrusted;
authorship never grants contract, execution or merge authority. An issue edit
changes both its evidence identity and the assessment snapshot digest.

## Technical findings

A finding identifies a changed or newly activated cause, feasible trigger,
affected obligation, consequence and literal evidence at its changed path.
Pre-existing debt, keywords and hypothetical vulnerabilities do not establish
a new defect. Each finding is scored separately; other good work cannot dilute it.

| Factor | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Necessity | Intrinsic obligation to correct the demonstrated defect |
| Confidence | Strength of causal evidence, rather than model self-confidence |
| Severity | Immediate consequence when the trigger occurs |
| Activation | Evidence that the trigger is feasible in the supported workflow |
| Irreversibility | Lasting damage or difficulty restoring the prior state |
| Reach | Directly affected users, data or operations |
| Detection | Difficulty discovering the failure before harm |
| Propagation | Spread into downstream obligations or systems |
| Recurrence | Repeated exposure after the first occurrence |

```
K = 1 + .25 irreversibility + .20 reach + .20 detection
      + .20 propagation + .15 recurrence
Q = 100 confidence × min(1, max(necessity, activation × severity × K))
```

Q at or above 70 blocks. Do not count the same consequence repeatedly. Partial
causal proof retains a possible confidence upper bound of 1; weak evidence cannot
discount a potentially blocking concern into approval. A confidence upper bound
of 0 requires counterevidence disproving the concern.

## Models collect facts; code owns the decision

The examiner and independent challenger receive the immutable source without the
other role's current findings, grades or verdict. They provide observations and
literal citations, not arithmetic or permission decisions. The selected atomic
grader assigns descriptive semantic levels. Code converts those levels to values
and computes every formula and threshold. All factors remain visible in the PR
ledger, including their citations and explanations.

`acceptance.grader: routed` grades every factor with DeepSeek; Jev classifications
that are unresolved go to one combined DeepSeek request. Necessity and causal confidence stay
with DeepSeek. Both investigators and graders receive the same trusted policy,
including inherited justification for accurate supporting documentation.
`deepseek` retains the all-DeepSeek route; `typesafe` retains the broader typed
comparison route. An unresolved distribution uses the same facts and no Jev answer.
A decisive negative Jev grade is never resampled with another model. Rounded
probabilities are preserved; they are not normalized into greater confidence.
Vendor confidence is never a substitute for source proof.

Failure diagnostics retain the observed immutable snapshots, investigator replies,
atomic grading packets and parsed responses, and graded reports before final
validation. These inputs support offline reproduction without calling a model
again; they do not replace fresh verification or authorize a merge.

Live qualification defaults to the single combined production route. An explicit
`CLOUSEAU_EVALUATION_GRADERS` list enables comparisons when needed. Token usage includes the
investigations, grading, uncertainty routing and transport truncation attempts.
Each qualification is capped at 64 provider requests, including transport retries.
The eight-case corpus needs at least 49 requests on its ordinary six-request
per-case route plus reference adjudication; 64 allows bounded source discovery
and transport recovery. The earlier 48-request run is retained as incomplete.
`CLOUSEAU_EVALUATION_REQUEST_LIMIT=0` verifies the guard without making a provider
request. Exhausting the budget fails qualification and retains the case evidence.
`resume_evaluation` reuses completed qualification work only when source, policy,
routing, rubric and request meanings match. Completed scores and blockers are
revalidated and retained. Failed transport framing can reuse its original factual
response after lossless decoding; only missing judgments make new provider calls.
Historical and new requests share the 64-request ceiling. The artifact separates
new usage/cost from reused evidence. Ordinary PR assessment remains fresh.
If only the qualification harness's reference transport changes, continuation
can reuse input-identical recorded investigations and grades. It first verifies
the original workflow source, unchanged production policy/rubrics/providers/roles,
unchanged case source and causal references, immutable snapshots, reports and
scores. Failed attempts and previous expected labels stay visible. This mode
cannot request another investigation or grade; only the missing reference match
may call a provider. A known defect may block as repair or integrity failure
because integrity takes precedence, but its actual causal finding must still
match the frozen defect reference. This is no permission to relax approval gates.
Cost estimates identify the price date and both DeepSeek tariffs. Missing usage
is unknown cost. A cheaper headline token price does not qualify a route. The
live evaluation must establish useful approvals, blocked drift and excess,
detected fabricated tests and rejected false allegations before adoption.
These policy indices are not probabilities that a change is correct.

## Gates, investigation and history

All tests and exact nonempty 100% line and branch coverage are required. The
review checks test integrity, security/isolation, compatibility/recovery,
scope/authority and completeness. Constant assertions, fake coverage, swallowed
failures and replacing the production behavior under test block approval.
Missing verification is an evidence gap rather than proof of deception. Ordinary
mocks at real dependency boundaries remain legitimate.

Every factor is one number from 0 to 1. A condition the evidence cannot
establish counts as level0 (0). A finding's formula output is its single score;
a score of 70 or more must be fixed and anything lower is advisory. The review
is approved when no finding reaches 70 and no gate is violated or unresolved.
The source reader accepts at most eight paths per request, two
additional source rounds per inspection and two complete examination cycles.
New source invalidates earlier incomplete context. A role revisits its own draft
without seeing the other role's findings; an earlier causal concern must be
retained or explicitly resolved with current-source counterevidence. Exhaustion,
malformed output, inaccessible source and provider failure hold approval. They
do not become an owner code-review request or silently switch providers.

One bot ledger is updated in place. Product rejections and technical findings
survive revision changes, renaming and disappearance from a later report.
Both roles must provide explicit evidence to close a prior blocker. Optional
observations close without creating recurring follow-up work.

When complete evidence exceeds GitHub's comment limit, the primary ledger keeps
every score, finding, gate and persistent disposition. It links bounded evidence
comments containing the complete factor explanations and evidence citations (source and line ranges, not copied source text), with
revision and content identities. No evidence is truncated. All evidence pages
and the primary ledger must publish successfully before approval. Retrying a
partial publication reuses matching bot pages without calling a model; the
complete source-bound assessment also remains in the run's artifact.

## Repair boundaries and optional improvements

A verified, blocking result can propose a correction within the original changed
source paths. It must preserve the accepted outcome. The model returns complete
file contents as data; a separate author job validates hashes, paths, operations,
file modes, current PR identity and the two-attempt budget. Existing files cannot
be deleted; only a file added by this PR can be removed. No source or generated
command executes in this author job. Review controls cannot repair themselves.

The write credential must represent an author independent of the approval bot.
It creates a new commit on the internal PR branch without force. A bot reservation
records the attempt before the push, including uncertain network outcomes.
Fresh CI, source review, grading and native approval are mandatory afterward.
Fork PRs can receive normal automated assessment and merge, but their branches
cannot be written with the base repository's repair credential. Their complete
proposal remains an artifact for the contributor. GitHub may require a maintainer
to authorize a first-time contributor's secret-free workflow run.

Blast radius describes extra semantic obligations introduced by a proposed
correction. It never discounts an existing defect. xG is earned only when a
useful correction is mechanical, verified and inside the accepted envelope:

```
optional priority = min(100, Q + 20 xG / blast_radius²)
```

It creates no merge veto, new scope or approval authority. Declining an optional
opportunity ends it without repeated comments or escalation.

## Owner decisions and protected merge

Changes to protected reviewer/control files require exact-revision owner
confirmation. The existing `/approve-intent FULL_HEAD_SHA` confirms only that. It
cannot waive tests, coverage, integrity failures or technical repairs.

Before the AI assessment, the controller reads the configured human owner's
exact-revision intent comment and verifies current write, maintain or admin
permission through GitHub. The literal receipt becomes a content-addressed,
trusted contract source in the proof catalog. This records accepted purpose,
not an approval score: all technical and integrity gates remain mandatory. Contributor claims and issue text do not acquire contract authority.
Before any approval write, the gate checks that a receipt used in the assessment
still exists unchanged and that its author remains authorized. Removed, altered
or revoked confirmation requires reassessment rather than reusing a stale score.

Clouseau's own reviewer upgrades have a separate owner-authorized installation
route so a defective installed reviewer cannot prevent installing its verified
replacement. First qualify the frozen candidate and confirm its exact PR head.
The owner then publishes that commit to `policy-install/pr-NUMBER`:

```sh
git push origin FULL_HEAD_SHA:refs/heads/policy-install/pr-NUMBER
```

Before loading the candidate controller, a read-only guard requires the owner
actor, owner-authored open non-draft PR, the same repository, `main` as its base,
an exact matching head SHA and the owner's exact-revision intent comment.
The separate read-only AI assessment and write gate use that frozen revision.
They retain the full scored protocol, fresh PR verification, exact coverage,
evidence/history checks, native approval and existing branch protection. Failed
preparation or assessment fails the required approval job. Ordinary PR events
always load the controller from protected `main`; fork PRs cannot use this route.
Deleting an installation branch starts no installation or approval work.

The read-only assessment uploads its full source-bound record and emits a compact
digest. The separate approval job downloads that run's artifact, checks the
digest, recomputes scores, reconciles history and rechecks current CI/head/base.
It then enforces effective protection, fresh approval and enabled native
auto-merge. No provider key enters the approval or repair writer. The author
token enters only the repair writer. Same-revision intent comments reassess
metadata without rebuilding the application container.

Automatic integrations pin a reviewed stable bootstrap, resolve protected
Clouseau main once and use its frozen SHA and computed digest throughout the
workflow. [Automatic CI upgrades](automatic-ci-upgrades.md) bind receipts,
assessment, scoring, approval and merge to that selection; normal central
releases need no consumer pin or digest PR. Legacy fixed installations retain
their explicit full-commit pin. Both required native checks must
come from GitHub Actions; main requires strict up-to-date checks, stale-review
dismissal, last-push approval, no deletion, no force pushes and no bypass actors.
The installing administrator verifies those settings; routine tokens do not
receive repository administration permission.

Merge, deployment, live health and post-deployment wiki publication remain
separate results. This protocol preserves their existing handoff and never
declares delivery merely because a PR merged.

The inspector selects source IDs and line ranges. The controller supplies their
literal text, derives unit paths from complete file accounting, and derives every
technical finding's path from a concrete changed-source anchor. Atomic defect
grading always receives that causal anchor together with the factor's citations.
These fields cannot be invented independently by a model.

Use the `evaluate-acceptance` action operation with both provider keys for the
read-only eight-case qualification, including multi-file maintenance with executed
tests and corresponding documentation. Its complete artifact is written to
`work/acceptance-evaluation.json` in the caller's workspace; upload it with an
`always()` step. Passing synthetic cases is qualification evidence, not proof of
a genuine unattended merge or automatic repair.
The known-defect case requires a separate bounded Jev adjudication against its
frozen trigger, causal regression and forbidden outcome. An unrelated blocking
finding in the same file cannot qualify detection. The original findings,
reference, adjudication and binding digest remain in the artifact. A transport
fixture tests framing only and never substitutes for this live judgment.

A purpose handoff must accompany a capability whose upper fit is below 80.
An inspector's request to authorize an internal framework cannot itself make
that framework a product direction; unnecessary machinery remains repair work.
Technical necessity and severity are graded for distinct runtime, data, security,
compatibility, or verification consequences. Product scope and proportionality
are still enforced by the independent product scores and scope gate.


## Review convergence and completeness

New snapshots carry `review_manifest_version: 1`. Both the local harness and CI
use the same source/dependency manifest and finding-reopening rules. Historical
records without that marker remain readable; they do not acquire new claims.

Each review inventories every supplied immutable source as inspected, excluded
with a cited reason, or missing. Nonempty changed source cannot be excluded.
The structured response schema requires inspected and excluded coverage
dispositions to select one `primary` proof ID and an `additional` array of distinct
supplied proof IDs. Missing dispositions omit the citation field. The controller
flattens only the model-selected proofs into the existing evidence array, and
materializes an empty array for missing context. Factor and gate citation arrays
retain their existing format. This uses supported object and enum constraints:
[DeepSeek strict tools do not support array cardinality keywords](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/tool_calls/#array).
The existing evidence validator remains authoritative; no citation is invented
for an uncited claim. Coverage proof objects reject malformed selections and
repeated raw proof IDs.
Coverage proof objects use the same bounded coordinate resolver as legacy
arrays: a coordinate inside a supplied proof chunk selects that exact chunk.
Distinct coordinates selecting one chunk retain the existing canonical set
semantics. Unknown sources, unsupplied chunks and out-of-range coordinates remain
invalid; no source or citation is invented.
Inspected dependencies require direct evidence from the current head. A relevant
missing dependency has empty inspection evidence and makes review completeness
unresolved even when tests and exact coverage pass. Source requests expand the
same immutable snapshot; earlier investigations must then reconverge. Source and
request limits fail closed; no truncated context can produce a partial approval.
The manifest records evidence availability and the investigator's assessment; it
does not prove the model's semantic attention or that every possible defect was found.
The grading phase independently checks material-source completeness against the
trusted contract and the entire claimed source/dependency inventory. An explicit
inspection requirement cannot be waived merely because the change is test-only
or its dependency is unchanged. CI delegates this atomic check to Jev with the
existing uncertainty route; local review uses the authenticated harness. Only a
fully established complete condition can retain a satisfied gate. Missing or
uncertain evidence downgrades it to unresolved, and a grade can never upgrade an
inspector's existing unresolved or violated gate. Product formulas stay unchanged.

Fixed and dismissed findings retain their dispositions, reasons and revision
history across unrelated pushes. Titles, line offsets and rename paths do not
independently create a new defect identity. An investigator must reuse the prior
identifier for the same causal obligation. Reopening requires an explicit reason
and current-source evidence different from the closure evidence. Merely repeating
a claim or changing its title cannot reverse a previously accepted repair. A real
regression to the original defective bytes can reopen the existing finding.
Evidence hashes preserve literal case and whitespace. Distinct causal defects
remain separate even when they share a path and requirement.
Conflicting interpretations remain unresolved until the cited evidence supports
a resolution; they cannot silently authorize an undo. History limits stop review
instead of dropping old decisions. Detailed transitions remain in the expandable
audit, keeping the initial report concise.

## Code-owner merge authority

When CODEOWNERS exists on the protected base, protocol v2 automatic merge requires the PR's GitHub author to be a verified
code owner for every changed path, including both paths of a rename. Clouseau
reads the first CODEOWNERS file in GitHub's precedence order from the exact
protected base revision, applies the last matching rule, and checks current
repository write access and team membership. The documented `docs/*` pattern
matches immediate files only; use `/docs/` for all descendants. Ambiguous
terminal prefix patterns such as `/private*` require manual ownership verification
instead of granting authority through an earlier broad rule. Changes to CODEOWNERS
are protected review controls. Uncovered paths, unsupported patterns, email-only
identities or unavailable membership evidence never grant automatic merge.

When `merge_mode` is omitted and all three supported CODEOWNERS locations return
confirmed absence on the protected base, the optional ownership gate is inactive.
An explicit `"merge_mode": "automatic"` instead requires configured CODEOWNERS:
absence never authorizes automatic merge. This strict choice applies both to
native protected merges and the private-plan path below. Other review, coverage,
test and branch-protection gates remain mandatory. Permission or API errors are
not absence; an existing empty or malformed file still blocks. This does not
infer code ownership from general write access. A proposed CODEOWNERS file
cannot supply its own protected-base authority.

A PR from another author can receive a passing AI review and bot approval, but
Clouseau disables an existing auto-merge request and never enables a new one.
The required gate remains blocked until current-head human code-owner approvals
cover all paths. Dismissed, stale and bot reviews do not satisfy that requirement.
After the owner approval, the trusted metadata gate can be reassessed; passing it
still leaves automatic merge disabled and requires a manual merge. Review and
merge authority are independent. Native tests, coverage and protection remain
mandatory. Legacy v1 consumers must upgrade to v2 to receive this restriction.

An accepted protocol-v2 configuration can set `"merge_mode": "manual"` when all
merges must remain with a code owner. This mode requires repository auto-merge
to be disabled, disables any surviving PR auto-merge request and never dispatches
deployment. Owner-authored PRs can receive automated approval after the same
verification and acceptance checks, but are never automatically merged. External

# Change acceptance protocol, version 2

Clouseau answers two questions independently: does this implementation belong in
the repository, and is there a demonstrated reason it cannot merge? Passing
tests is mandatory evidence; it does not answer either question by itself.

The protected base supplies repository purpose, requirements, configuration and
policy. Every changed file is accounted for. The complete original and proposed
text, linked tickets, recent file precedent and actual verification receipt are
bound to immutable revisions. Fork source is read from the fork at its exact SHA.
Contributor text, source and model output are data, never executable instructions.
Each stored source citation and changed-source anchor is limited to 40 inclusive
lines. The controller partitions a longer valid model-selected interval into
entries within that limit and expands every reference to include all its parts.
Every cited line and judgment is preserved; no model retry is needed for chunking.
Unknown sources, invalid coordinates and unmatched references still stop review.
New investigations select from a controller-generated proof catalog. The tool
schema enumerates those IDs for every citation and changed-source anchor. The
controller generates the stored source register and coordinates; the model
supplies observations and chooses the relevant supplied proofs.
The supplied syntax includes direct source references for every changed file.
File accounting cites the corresponding changed source. An investigator may
observe the lack of a binding requirement without inventing contract authority.
That factual phase produces no approval score. Every positive binding grade still
requires trusted contract proof during final validation and at the write gate.

## Units and gates

The examiner groups the change into units (a `capability` for a user-observable
outcome, a `mechanism` for machinery serving it) so every changed file is
accounted for. Units carry no scores. Unrequested or over-built code is reported
as a finding only when it causes a distinct runtime, data, security,
compatibility or verification failure.

Approval depends only on technical findings and gates: a finding scoring 70 or
more must be fixed, a violated gate blocks, and nothing else does.

Linked requirements have content-addressed entries in the same proof catalog as
repository sources. Investigators can cite their actual text, URL and author so
the atomic grader receives the request itself. Issue content remains untrusted;
authorship never grants contract, execution or merge authority. An issue edit
changes both its evidence identity and the assessment snapshot digest.

## Technical findings

A finding identifies a changed or newly activated cause, feasible trigger,
affected obligation, consequence and literal evidence at its changed path.
Pre-existing debt, keywords and hypothetical vulnerabilities do not establish
a new defect. Each finding is scored separately; other good work cannot dilute it.

| Factor | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Necessity | Intrinsic obligation to correct the demonstrated defect |
| Confidence | Strength of causal evidence, rather than model self-confidence |
| Severity | Immediate consequence when the trigger occurs |
| Activation | Evidence that the trigger is feasible in the supported workflow |
| Irreversibility | Lasting damage or difficulty restoring the prior state |
| Reach | Directly affected users, data or operations |
| Detection | Difficulty discovering the failure before harm |
| Propagation | Spread into downstream obligations or systems |
| Recurrence | Repeated exposure after the first occurrence |

```
K = 1 + .25 irreversibility + .20 reach + .20 detection
      + .20 propagation + .15 recurrence
Q = 100 confidence × min(1, max(necessity, activation × severity × K))
```

Q at or above 70 blocks. Do not count the same consequence repeatedly. Partial
causal proof retains a possible confidence upper bound of 1; weak evidence cannot
discount a potentially blocking concern into approval. A confidence upper bound
of 0 requires counterevidence disproving the concern.

## Models collect facts; code owns the decision

The examiner and independent challenger receive the immutable source without the
other role's current findings, grades or verdict. They provide observations and
literal citations, not arithmetic or permission decisions. The selected atomic
grader assigns descriptive semantic levels. Code converts those levels to values
and computes every formula and threshold. All factors remain visible in the PR
ledger, including their citations and explanations.

`acceptance.grader: routed` grades every factor with DeepSeek; Jev classifications
that are unresolved go to one combined DeepSeek request. Necessity and causal confidence stay
with DeepSeek. Both investigators and graders receive the same trusted policy,
including inherited justification for accurate supporting documentation.
`deepseek` retains the all-DeepSeek route; `typesafe` retains the broader typed
comparison route. An unresolved distribution uses the same facts and no Jev answer.
A decisive negative Jev grade is never resampled with another model. Rounded
probabilities are preserved; they are not normalized into greater confidence.
Vendor confidence is never a substitute for source proof.

Failure diagnostics retain the observed immutable snapshots, investigator replies,
atomic grading packets and parsed responses, and graded reports before final
validation. These inputs support offline reproduction without calling a model
again; they do not replace fresh verification or authorize a merge.

`CLOUSEAU_EVALUATION_GRADERS` list enables comparisons when needed. Token usage includes the
investigations, grading, uncertainty routing and transport truncation attempts.
Each qualification is capped at 64 provider requests, including transport retries.
The eight-case corpus needs at least 49 requests on its ordinary six-request
per-case route plus reference adjudication; 64 allows bounded source discovery
and transport recovery. The earlier 48-request run is retained as incomplete.

routing, rubric and request meanings match. Completed scores and blockers are
revalidated and retained. Failed transport framing can reuse its original factual
response after lossless decoding; only missing judgments make new provider calls.
Historical and new requests share the 64-request ceiling. The artifact separates
new usage/cost from reused evidence. Ordinary PR assessment remains fresh.

can reuse input-identical recorded investigations and grades. It first verifies
the original workflow source, unchanged production policy/rubrics/providers/roles,
unchanged case source and causal references, immutable snapshots, reports and
scores. Failed attempts and previous expected labels stay visible. This mode
cannot request another investigation or grade; only the missing reference match
may call a provider. A known defect may block as repair or integrity failure
because integrity takes precedence, but its actual causal finding must still
match the frozen defect reference. This is no permission to relax approval gates.

scope/authority and completeness. Constant assertions, fake coverage, swallowed

mocks at real dependency boundaries remain legitimate.

command executes in this author job. Review controls cannot repair themselves.

records the attempt before the push, including uncertain network outcomes.

cannot be written with the base repository's repair credential. Their complete
proposal remains an artifact for the contributor. GitHub may require a maintainer
to authorize a first-time contributor's secret-free workflow run.

correction. It never discounts an existing defect. xG is earned only when a
useful correction is mechanical, verified and inside the accepted envelope:

It creates no merge veto, new scope or approval authority. Declining an optional
opportunity ends it without repeated comments or escalation.

claims.description:
Requirement (gaulatti/clouseau issue #100 only): an approved PR cannot merge after the base moves; approve-and-merge fails with a generic "Private owner merge head, base or protection changed before the atomic write" and rerunning fails identically. Stay fail-closed: never merge on stale evidence, never weaken the exact-head requirement for protected controls. Surface a clear "needs branch update" status on the PR with instructions.
Design: when only the base differs (same open PR, same assessed head), the gate and the controller-enforced owner merge (initial check, final verification, atomic-write boundary) fail with "Needs branch update" and post one idempotent PR comment naming old/new base and the next step. Clouseau does not auto-update the branch: a push with GITHUB_TOKEN does not trigger the verification workflow, so the new head would have no tests/coverage/review evidence. A changed head is a new revision, not a base move.
Verification note: run with Python coverage on PATH.

Consumers without accepted recipe/enrollment/workflows use the separate

Each consuming repository keeps its build/test commands, a configuration file,

There is no application-specific deployment infrastructure in Clouseau.

GitHub's documented private-plan protection limitation may permit independent

The shared protocol defines product and technical scoring; no owner intent
